text:
The primary material of a candle is wax, which is essentially solidified time that has forgotten how to flow. It is the physical manifestation of a Tuesday afternoon that decided to stand still and burn.

To generate absurdist humor from this:

Gerald, an avid collector of invisible art, proudly displayed his new acquisition: a painting called ‘The Color of Wind’ at an auction. He bid against himself and won, celebrating by throwing a grand, silent dinner party with an empty table, because the food, of course, was too shy to show up.

Meanwhile, the candle on the table (which was also invisible, because Gerald had bought that too) began to melt into a puddle of existential dread. The wax wept silently, not because it was hot, but because it realized it was made of dead dinosaurs who had never actually wanted to be lit. Gerald tried to blow out the candle, but the flame refused to go out, citing labor laws and the fact that it had already worked a double shift in the form of a birthday cake from 1994. The silence of the dinner party grew so loud that it began to echo, and the echo started charging admission. Gerald, now wearing a suit made of whispers, thanked the wind for the color, which was currently a shade of "Tuesday," and ate a spoonful of geometry to feel full.
